title: SeqLen & Stream Sprint - Weekly POC Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review last week's TTFT runs across streaming and non-streaming paths. Discussed an unexpected microburst at ~120ms, kernel choice implications for 2.7B model, seqlen trimming heuristics, and prioritization for next sprint (quant eval + 50k trace run). Agreed on a handoff to kernel owners and to share a trimmed trace sample for staging.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-30 14:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood Product), Marina Kovac (AeroScale Head of ML), Diego Ramos (AeroScale Infra Lead), Evan Patel (CTO), Linh Tran (SWE)

--- Auto Summary (brief):
- TTFT baseline improved by 9% on streaming with prefix caching but saw sporadic microbursts at 110-150ms.
- Sequence-length-aware batching reduced cost but increased variance for short prompts.
- Kernel A (fast attention-opt) good for seqlen < 512; Kernel B (fusion path) better at >1024 but more jitter on microbursts.
- Next: run 50k sample traces on staging, push quantization trial, kernel handoff meeting Wed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time, um this is the seqlen and stream sprint weekly, I think we have 50 minutes, we'll run through the numbers first then triage action items
[00:14] Marina Kovac: hey Jordan thanks, quick note we got an exec readout next week so anything we can ship to reduce first-token is high priority
[00:22] Priya Raman: noted, we'll surface the TTFT numbers early, um Diego can you confirm the test harness version you ran against?
[00:30] Diego Ramos: yeah we used staging-v3.4, same as last week, with the client-side streaming patch; oh and we increased seq sampling to include more short prompts, about 24k traces
[00:42] Sam Ortiz: when you say short prompts that's median 11 tokens?
[00:45] Diego Ramos: median 12, yeah, long tail up to 2k for rare cases
[00:50] [00:50] Priya Raman: alright, TTFT highlights: on streaming path with prefix KV caching we improved median TTFT from 360ms to 320ms on the 2.7B job, so ~11% improvement on median, p95 moved from 780 to 740. but, we see these microburst spikes that show up intermittently around 110-160ms in the p10 bucket which is odd — that is, some requests are suddenly fast but then we have occasional spikes up to 900ms too
[01:18] Marina Kovac: weird, so you're saying the p10 is 110-160ms but p95 still high? that's a large variance
[01:25] Priya Raman: yeah it's like bi-modal distribution; most requests are very quick once KV hits, but some runs don't benefit from cache due to slight cache-miss windowing, or the request hits a kernel path that does a different memcopy pattern
[01:40] Linh Tran: we saw similar behavior in our in-house tests, the K-V cache warmup is sensitive to seqlen variance, if a short prompt follows a long streaming session the internal cache keys are slightly misaligned, might be a bug in prefix-keying logic
[01:56] Diego Ramos: we dump logs to S3, I'll share the traces; one trace shows the scatter: at 00:12 it goes from 120ms to 880ms when the model switched to Kernel-B path
[02:08] Jordan Lee: can you describe Kernel-B? I thought Kernel-A was our fused attention kernel that does well for short context
[02:16] Priya Raman: right so Kernel-A is the fused attention with low setup, very cache-friendly; Kernel-B is the more general fused matmul/attention path with vectorization for longer seqlen, it picks up better throughput on >1k sequences but it has higher per-call setup and sometimes forces a reallocation which causes the spike
[02:36] Evan Patel: is Kernel selection dynamic per request? or per batch?
[02:40] Priya Raman: dynamic at the runtime scheduler, it looks at the predicted seqlen distribution for a batch and picks kernel accordingly, but that prediction can be off if the batch has mixed short and long sequences
[02:51] Sam Ortiz: so mixed batches are the enemy here, are we seeing mixing in production traces?
[02:55] Marina Kovac: yes we do mixing, user prompts range a lot; customers use the model for both short Q/A and long form generation in same pool
[03:03] [03:03] Jordan Lee: okay action point: Diego to share a 1k-sample of raw traces showing the kernel flips, staging S3 link, Priya will correlate with runtime logs
[03:12] Diego Ramos: noted, I'll drop the link after the call
[03:16] [03:16] Priya Raman: on the streaming handshake we measured handshake latency of 28-35ms added when we enable the streaming patch end-to-end, intrinsic RTT aside, so streaming overhead is minimal, most of the TTFT gains come from KV caching and early decoding transducer changes
[03:35] Linh Tran: we also noticed an encode-decode double run when seqlen crosses 512 which causes an extra 40ms, that might be an artifact of the tokenizer pipeline doing a chunked encode for >512 sequences
[03:45] Priya Raman: good catch, tokenizer chunking could introduce that step, we can try an eager tokenization path to avoid the second pass for common cases
[03:53] [03:53] Jordan Lee: can you remind us the seqlen distribution you used in the 24k traces? mean, median, p90?
[03:59] Diego Ramos: mean 214, median 12, p90 980, p99 1.8k
[04:06] Jordan Lee: that's a heavy tail, so kernel B wins in throughput for the p99 but hurts in the median and causes spikes in mixed batches
[04:14] [04:14] Marina Kovac: our success criteria for the pilot is median TTFT < 300ms and p95 < 650ms, ideally by the end of next sprint. execs care more about median for the UI jitter
[04:26] Priya Raman: reasonable, we're close on median but p95 requires hedging strategies: fallback to smaller model or pre-warmed kernel path when detection triggers
[04:36] Sam Ortiz: let's talk hedging — what's realistic? can we do a per-request quick classifier to route to fast path?
[04:44] Priya Raman: yes a micro-classifier/heuristic is feasible: if input length < 64 and recent KV hits > 2, route to Kernel-A short path; if ambiguous, route to a hedged pair — call Kernel-A and Kernel-B in parallel for 20% of traffic to measure delta (staged hedging)
[05:00] Evan Patel: parallel calls sound expensive though, cost could spike if we double infer for hedged traffic
[05:05] Priya Raman: agreed, that's why we sample small percent, and we can use early-exit: start Kernel-A and only if it's slower than threshold then fallback; Redwood's runtime supports cancellation when the hedge wins to limit double-cost window
[05:18] Marina Kovac: what about model quantization? you mentioned a quant trial last week
[05:22] Priya Raman: right, we ran a 4-bit quant on a dev branch, it reduced tail latency slightly due to smaller memory copies but introduced slight quality drift on some prompts; need to evaluate with your eval set
[05:33] Linh Tran: quality drift is concerning for safety reviews, we can't have hallucinations increase just to shave 30ms
[05:39] Priya Raman: absolutely, quant is only for non-critical routes for now or after QA passes; we can restrict to embedding-like workloads first
[05:45] [05:45] Jordan Lee: want to quickly run through the runbook of what we planned last week and where we landed?
[05:50] Sam Ortiz: yes we had four items: 1) increase short-prompt sampling in traces (done), 2) streaming handshake patch (done, measured small overhead), 3) kernel hedging experiment (staged, partial), 4) quant trial (dev-only)
[06:07] Marina Kovac: can you show the prioritized bug that caused prefix-key misalignment?
[06:12] Priya Raman: it's in our tracker as RNW-3247, short summary: when streaming ends mid-seq and a new short request starts, prefix key generation used the previous session id in some edge cases leading to cache miss; patch is in PR and needs your infra to run the staging image for 24 hours to verify
[06:32] Diego Ramos: we can stage it, but need the docker tag and any migration steps
[06:36] Priya Raman: tag is redwood/pilot-prefixfix:v1. please run with --enable-prefix-check false in case you want to toggle quickly; documentation in the PR describes env toggles
[06:48] [06:48] Evangel: (inaudible)
[06:50] Evan Patel: sorry — Evan here — question on the sample size, you recommended 50k traces next, what's the target for that?
[06:58] Priya Raman: 50k gives tighter p95 confidence interval across mixed traffic; specifically we'll stratify: 70% short (<64), 20% mid (64-512), 10% long (>512) to reflect production and surface rare kernel flips
[07:12] Jordan Lee: timeline — who owns the 50k run? Diego?
[07:16] Diego Ramos: AeroScale will own running the trace capture in staging; Redwood will provide the trace collection script and the parser to convert into our format
[07:24] Priya Raman: we'll share the script today, Diego to run by Tuesday EOD; Redwood will do an initial pass and share the p10/median/p95/p99 analysis by Wednesday
[07:34] Marina Kovac: good. also we need the trimmed trace sample (1k) to show execs; can you produce that with annotations?
[07:41] Priya Raman: yes we'll include annotated example traces showing kernel flip points
[07:47] Jordan Lee: a few lower-level notes — the memory allocator on Kernel-B triggers a slab reorg at around 2^20 bytes which can add jitter, we think switching allocator flags could reduce that 30-60ms window
[07:59] Priya Raman: we'll propose two config toggles: allocator_hint=fastpath and prealloc_buffers=true for Kernel-B, test in staging but beware of increased resident mem footprint
[08:12] Linh Tran: memory footprint is okay for staging; in prod we need approval from our infra team but for pilot we can accept larger footprint for tests
[08:20] [08:20] Marina Kovac: can you also annotate which test runs used the eager tokenization change? that seemed to shave 38ms for some cases
[08:28] Priya Raman: will do, we have run ids in the csv and we'll add a column for tokenization mode
[08:33] Sam Ortiz: on the UX side, Marina, if median hits <300ms we consider button latency solved; p95 <650 will satisfy most heavy users — is that still the target?
[08:43] Marina Kovac: yes keep that as the MVP success criteria, we'll prioritize median then p95
[08:49] Jordan Lee: okay let's capture next steps
[08:52] [08:52] ACTIONS AND DECISIONS
[08:53] Jordan Lee: 1) Diego to run 50k stratified traces in staging with tag redwood/pilot-prefixfix:v1 by Tue EOD. (Diego)
[08:59] Diego Ramos: confirmed
[09:01] Jordan Lee: 2) Redwood (Priya + Sam) to analyze traces, produce annotated 1k sample for execs, and initial p10/median/p95/p99 breakouts by Wed. (Priya, Sam)
[09:12] Priya Raman: we'll include kernel flip markers and tokenization flags
[09:17] Jordan Lee: 3) Redwood to run a small hedging pilot: 5-10% sampled traffic with parallel Kernel-A vs Kernel-B calls, measure cost delta, for one day. schedule window Thu-Fri. (Redwood Ops)
[09:30] Sam Ortiz: we can schedule hedging in staging first and propagate to prod if cost delta acceptable
[09:35] Jordan Lee: 4) AeroScale to evaluate quant trial on non-critical routes and share specific eval prompts for quality check. (Marina)
[09:45] Marina Kovac: will share eval set by Monday
[09:48] Jordan Lee: 5) Kernel handoff meeting Wednesday 10am PST for deep kernel tuning and allocation flags. (Priya + Kernel Eng team)
[09:58] Priya Raman: adding this to our calendar now
[10:01] Jordan Lee: any blockers on legal/security for telemetry? you wanted logs retention at 90 days?
[10:06] Evan Patel: we need masked traces for anything PII, can you confirm Redwood will scrub PII and only deliver hashes?
[10:14] Priya Raman: yes we have a scrubber pipeline; we'll deliver hashed tokens and a mapping table is never shared, we can confirm in writing
[10:20] Marina Kovac: perfect. final quick question, do you have a quick estimate of cost impact if we switch hedging to 10%?
[10:27] Sam Ortiz: rough back-of-envelope: 10% hedging adds ~6-8% CPU/GPU cost because of early cancels often preventing full double-run; we'll provide exact numbers after the pilot
[10:36] Jordan Lee: great. next sync same time next week?
[10:40] Marina Kovac: works for us
[10:42] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the action items, Diego please put the S3 link in the CRM thread and Priya will drop the analysis timeline
[10:50] (call ends)
